summary: Takayasu Suzuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1983 to 1987. He served as a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University (attested 2014–2015).

Takayoshi Kamei (1886–1977) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He taught Hajime Nakamura and held posts at the University of Tokyo, Ibaraki University (c. 1949–1957), and Seisen University (c. 1957).

Takayoshi Namikawa (born 1947) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Bukkyo University. He was appointed professor there in 1981 and emeritus professor in 2018, also holding posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University and Hokkaido University.

Takayuki Hirosawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served at Taisho University as a group member until 1991 and was attested as a professor there in 2014.

Takehiro Sueki (1921–2007) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (c. 1941–1944). He held posts at the University of Electro-Communications (c. 1953–1969), the University of Tokyo (c. 1969–1982), and Toyo University (c. 1982–1992).

Takeo Hibino (1914–2007) was a historian, archaeologist, and sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (c. 1933–1936). He held posts at Kyoto University from 1936 to 1977, Otemon Gakuin University (1977), and Otemae University (1980).

Takeo Kanaseki (1897–1983) was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1919 to 1923. He held posts at Kyushu University (c. 1949–1960), Tottori University (c. 1960–1964), and Tezukayama Gakuin University (c. 1964–1979).

Takeshi Fujii (born 1955) is an Indologist and historian who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi. He taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from 1987, becoming professor in 2001 and emeritus professor in 2021.

Takeshi Hasegawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a teaching post at Ryukoku University (attested 1998) and lecturer posts attested in 2026 at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Takeshi Karashima (1903–1967) was a sinologist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (c. 1924–1927). He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (c. 1930–1945), Sagami Women's University, Showa Women's University, and Kamakura's library.

Takeshi Umehara (1925–2019) was a philosopher and Japanologist who studied at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held posts at Ritsumeikan University, Kyoto City University of Arts, the International Research Center for Japanese Studies, and the Institute of Technologists.

Takeshiro Kuraishi (1897–1975) was a sinologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo (c. 1918–1921). He was a professor at Kyoto University (c. 1939–1949), taught at the University of Tokyo (c. 1949–1958), and headed Chugokugo Gakkai (c. 1951–1974).

Takezo Kaneko (1905–1987) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (c. 1925–1928). He held posts at Hokkaido University (c. 1940–1947), the University of Tokyo (c. 1947–1966), and International Christian University (c. 1966).

Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche (1926–2015) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé and taught Phakchok Rinpoche. He succeeded Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö in 2012.

Taku Fukuda (born 1963) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Hajime Sakurabe. He held a post at Doho University beginning in 1995 and was attested in 2026 at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Takudo Ishikawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He served as a research fellow at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005–2006) and held teaching appointments at Taisho University (attested 2015 and 2026).

Takushu Sugimoto (born 1935) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology, having earned his degrees at Tohoku University. He held professorships at Kanazawa University, Komazawa University, and Kinjo University, becoming emeritus professor at Kanazawa circa 2000.
Tamala Krishna Gosvami (1946–2002) worked in religious studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Cambridge under the supervision of Julius Lipner.
Tamar Reich is an Indologist who held academic posts attested at the University of Chicago in 1996 and at the University of Calgary in 2003.
Tamara Cohen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed her PhD at the University of Toronto in 2023 under the supervision of Srilata Raman and Jürgen Hanneder.
